title: Response Attack: Exploiting Contextual Priming to Jailbreak Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2507.05248v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Contextual priming, where earlier stimuli covertly bias later judgments, offers an unexplored attack surface for large language models (LLMs). We uncover a contextual priming vulnerability in which the previous response in the dialogue can steer its subsequent behavior toward policy-violating content. While existing jailbreak attacks largely rely on single-turn or multi-turn prompt manipulations, or inject static in-context examples, these methods suffer from limited effectiveness, inefficiency, or semantic drift. We introduce Response Attack (RA), a novel framework that strategically leverages intermediate, mildly harmful responses as contextual primers within a dialogue. translated_title: 响应攻击：利用上下文启动效应越狱大语言模型
translated_abstract: 上下文启动效应（contextual priming）是指先前的刺激会隐蔽地影响后续的判断，这为大语言模型（LLM）提供了一个尚未被探索的攻击面。我们揭示了一种上下文启动漏洞：对话中的前一个响应可以将模型的后续行为引向违反政策的内容。现有的越狱攻击主要依赖于单轮或多轮的提示词操纵，或注入静态的上下文示例，这些方法存在效果有限、效率低下或语义漂移等问题。我们提出了响应攻击（Response Attack, RA），这是一种新颖的框架，它在对话中策略性地利用中间产生的轻度有害响应作为上下文启动器。通过重新表述有害查询，并在发出目标触发提示之前注入这些中间响应，RA利用了LLM中一个此前被忽视的漏洞。在八个最先进的大语言模型上进行的大量实验表明，RA始终能够实现……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文提出“响应攻击”（RA）框架，通过在对话中策略性地将中间产生的轻度有害响应作为上下文启动器，再发出触发提示，从而利用上下文启动效应这一此前被忽视的漏洞实现对大语言模型的越狱。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Response Attack (RA), a novel jailbreak framework that strategically uses intermediate mildly harmful responses as contextual primers before issuing a trigger prompt, exploiting a previously overlooked contextual priming vulnerability in large language models.
